For years, Donald Trump has fetishized deadly war crimes, and also the allure
and entertainment value of public executions. On both fronts, Pete Hegseth -
the former 'Fox & Friends Weekend' co-host and current so-called "secretary of
war" - has been the president's premier errand boy.

Since January 2025, when he ascended to the top of the Pentagon despite a
deluge of [scandal and allegations](https://zeteo.com/p/pete-hegseth-asks-
mommy-to-help-clean) that nearly sank his nomination, Hegseth has towered
above the rest of Trump 2.0's cabinet secretaries as the appointee most eager
to quench Trump's incessant bloodlust and desires for regional conquest and
lawless, brutal domination of his enemies, foreign and domestic.

Hegseth has at times proposed actions that go too far, even for Trump, whose
baying for blood is sporadically tempered by his own cowardice. Perhaps the
most grisly example of Hegseth out-Trumping the sadistically maximalist
president took place over the past week, after the Trump-Vance administration
announced it would stage not only the first official public execution in the
U.S. in nearly a century, but the first one streamed live on the internet.
Hegseth [argued](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hegseth-fort-hood-shooter-
execution-public-nidal-hasan/) it was necessary because "people need to
understand that there's serious consequences."

Trump approved this vile plan, but apparently didn't know some key details,
people familiar with the matter tell **Zeteo** : Namely, the convicted mass
murderer slated to be executed in December is partly paralyzed and confined to
a wheelchair. "He's in a fucking wheelchair?" Trump privately exclaimed,
telling people that Hegseth never told him that and that killing an old guy in
a wheelchair might not look cool.

Suddenly, reports [trickled](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/13/politics/trump-
fort-hood-shooter-livestream-execution) out that the plan to broadcast the
execution was in jeopardy. Trump announced Thursday morning the livestream is
off - "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch," he said
- though the execution will move forward. This shambolic episode of will-they-
won't-they, when it comes to broadcasting real-time footage of a military
snuff film, is a perfect distillation of what Hegseth has done as defense
secretary, under the watchful gaze and direction of the Trump White House, to
the Pentagon in relatively short order.

Hegseth has operationalized the president's core demands for gun-brandishing
spite, boastful bigotry, naked imperialism, and violent spectacle - and the
former Fox host is using every lever of the U.S. military and its civilian
command to bring Trump's vindictive, MAGA-branded militarism to life, abroad
and at home.

When Hegseth pitched the idea for livestreaming Nidal Hasan's execution by
military firing squad, he wasn't freelancing. He was just giving Trump what
the president had been telling his team he wanted - for more than a decade, at
least.
